remainingEvidence: A dispatcher declares only the record kinds it owns itself, so a command family's own records sit inside the set the gate protects but outside the declaration it compares. src/protocol/dispatcher.ts#CommandDispatcher declares the write record and the audit record, and src/actors/actor.ts#Actor adds the recovery carrier; a Run commit, a slot entry and a materialization plan are none of those. Closing it needs a declaration member on src/protocol/registration.ts#ProtocolCommand, which is W1's file, and a value on every registered command, which is not: src/protocol/run-commands.ts is W5's, src/protocol/facet-commands.ts is W3's and src/protocol/materialization-commands.ts is W4's. The member is left absent rather than added empty, because a command that declares nothing would read as a command that owns no records

That gap is not hypothetical and now has a dated instance. W4's treeMerge cutover moved five definition codec majors in one change — definition.blueprint 2 to 3, definition.managed-state 2 to 3, definition.actor-plan 1 to 2, definition.materialization-plan 1 to 2 and definition.materialization-rollout 1 to 2 — and src/protocol/dispatcher.ts#CommandDispatcher names none of the five, so a store written before that cutover would be refused by each row's own codec on the way past rather than by the declaration a reader reaches first. That is exactly the discovery-by-decoding this rule exists to replace, and it is the case the ProtocolCommand declaration member above would have caught

The three derivations §8.3 names as the reason totality matters are each owed as a case that rejects rather than answering short, and each belongs to the wave that owns the derivation: reserved-minus-completed under C13-RUN-FRONTIER-COMPLETE, an ancestry walk under C13-RUN-ANCESTRY and the settlement test under C13-RUN-SETTLED-DERIVED are all W5 rows in runs-turns.json. Naming a foreign atom is not owing its evidence. The mechanism those cases would exercise is the src/actors/actor.ts#Actor gate this row already evidences on both substrates, so each is a citation W5 adds rather than a mechanism anyone still has to build
bounds: The bootstrap is deliberately two carriers rather than one, because a declaration inside the record a reader must decode first cannot be reached before decoding. src/actors/fence.ts#ActorRecoveryState stays at codec 1.0 and carries only the Actor, the fence epoch and the recovery count, so an immediately older reader still constructs and fences. The declaration lives beside it as raw canonical JSON with no RecordCodec envelope, written and read through ActorStore#saveRecordSetDeclaration and #loadRecordSetDeclaration, which is why a future or malformed declaration produces a constructible Actor that refuses every operation instead of a construction failure. The raw form is by design, not an omission: an envelope over the declaration would reintroduce the record whose version is the thing in dispute

The declaration carrier is constituent ActorStore state and not a second owner. It commits and rolls back inside the same activation transaction as the recovery record on both substrates — the Memory draft in src/actors/store.ts#MemoryActorStore and the actor_record_set_declaration row in src/substrates/sqlite/actor.ts#SqliteActorStore — and an older snapshot or database carrying no declaration reads as the empty declaration rather than as a fault

The declaration is durable state without being a registry record, and that is a claim about custody rather than an omission. src/core/codec.ts#CodecDeclaration has no RecordCodec and therefore no wire kind, so artifacts/records has nothing to classify it under: scripts/quality/codec-records.mjs#codecKind derives a kind only from a static codec member or from a static encode that delegates to one, and this carrier delegates to canonical JSON instead. Its statics are named toBytes and fromBytes for exactly that reason, so encode and decode keep meaning 'through this record's own codec' and the record registry does not discover a codec-bearing class that has no codec. Custody is the owning Actor's, discharged through the actor.recovery-state row's own store seam, and the declaration bytes never derive a durable identity

A refused activation still advances the Actor fence epoch. Fencing a stale incarnation is a §8.1 obligation rather than part of the record set §8.3 leaves untouched, so this rule claims that the stored declaration bytes and the records they name are unchanged, which the cited tests assert directly, and claims nothing about the fence epoch

The declaration is compared once per activation and the verdict is captured, rather than re-read before each operation. A declaration rewritten underneath a live Actor by something that is not a reader is therefore outside this rule, and it is already a separate violation: §8.4 rule 1 gives every record type exactly one owning Actor

The Cloudflare profile keeps its own mechanism. packages/agent-core-cloudflare/src/migration.ts remains the release-distance specialisation of this rule, and this row claims only the substrate-level obligation, never any part of C13-CLOUDFLARE-ROLLBACK-WINDOW, which stays W8's to evidence

A substrate schema marker is a specialisation of this rule rather than a second mechanism, and the same reading applies beyond the Cloudflare profile: W4's SQLite MATERIALIZATION_SCHEMA_VERSION moving 2 to 3 refuses an old database at the marker instead of at the first row that fails to decode, which is this rule's timing obligation applied to one table family. This row claims the Actor-owned record set and never a substrate's own migration marker, so a marker and a declaration coexisting is not a duplicated plane

remainingEvidence: Registration and release remain owed for 17 of the 24 declared durable kinds, none of them in a file W1 may write. Closed here: src/content/retention.ts#ContentRetention is the seam, src/content/memory.ts#MemoryContentRetention and src/substrates/sqlite/content-retention.ts#SqliteContentRetention are its two implementations, and one parameterised body in test/content/retention-contract.ts runs create, replace, rollback, restart, release, append-only retention, collection exclusion with two owner keys on one ContentRef, repeated and concurrent collection passes, and the transient lease hold against both. Closed by W5 with nothing further owed: src/agents/runs/store.ts projects run.commit, turn.record, run.checkpoint, turn.inbox-entry and run.spawn-reservation onto ContentOwnerEdge values, reconciles them through reconcileContentCustody inside the same insert or replace transaction, and re-verifies the exact owner namespace on activation through verifyContentCustody. The registry now declares 31 ContentRef-bearing kinds rather than 30: 24 durable records and 7 value records, the value records naming fields while correctly claiming no independent durable retainer

W7 owes registration and release for four kinds and holds the only rival mechanism: workspace.event (src/workspaces/event.ts#Event), workspace.route-reservation and workspace.route-projection (src/workspaces/route.ts) and workspace.content-retention-reference (src/workspaces/retention.ts). src/workspaces/retention.ts#ContentRetentionPort declares verify, release and discard but no retain, and no file under src implements it, so no W7 write path registers content today and no W7 removal path releases it into a ContentRetention

W8 owes registration and release for ten kinds, and no file under src/slates or src/environments references ContentOwnerEdge or ContentRetention today: slate (src/slates/slate.ts), slate.version (src/slates/version.ts), slate.preview (src/slates/preview.ts), slate.resource (src/slates/resource.ts), slate.publication (src/slates/publication.ts), slate.deployment (src/slates/deployment.ts), slate.resource-reservation and slate.deployment-reservation (src/slates/store.ts), environment.revision (src/environments/environment.ts) and environment.snapshot (src/environments/snapshot.ts)

W4 owes registration and release for definition.package-release and definition.metadata-snapshot (src/definition/package.ts), whose declared retention owner is the Tenant, and W6 owes registration for invocation.receipt (src/invocations/receipt.ts), which this document declares append-only, so W6 owes retention on write and never a release. Neither src/definition nor src/invocations references ContentOwnerEdge or ContentRetention today

The nested definition and Environment references and the inherited AttemptReceipt.result case this row named before belong to W4, W8 and W6 together with those kinds. A W1 slice cannot write them, because the retaining record and its write path are in those waves' files, and §8.4 rule 1 gives each of those record types exactly one owning Actor outside W1
bounds: Content put into a ContentStore and not yet named by any record is never offered for collection, because the seam refuses to collect a blob that has no Tenant relation at all, which keeps a writer's bytes alive between put and retain and leaves reclamation of never-named content outside this rule

Custody is single-Actor. A ContentStore and its retention state are bound to exactly one Tenant and Actor per §8.4 rule 1 and every edge from a foreign Tenant or Actor is refused before any mutation, so this rule never claims that two Actors can share retention of one ContentRef

Tenant retention policy is consulted, never implemented. The seam asks a TenantContentPolicyReader about each candidate and fails closed on an absent, denied or faulting answer, so export, legal deletion and Tenant closure stay the policy owner's obligation and outside this rule

This rule does not claim that every guard inside collect is independently load-bearing. The owner checks in the candidate scan are redundant with the relation invariant that owned content always carries a null tombstone, which both implementations assert on every read, so removing either alone changes no observable behaviour and no cited test can discriminate it

bounds: Determinism is measured across hosts, not across runs. Twelve cases run on the memory and SQLite compositions agree case by case including on the envelope digest, so the two hosts are shown to have decided the same bytes rather than merely to have produced the same labels, and the observed outcome set equals the exact declared CommandOutcome union. Not measured: repeated runs of one host, and concurrent interleaving of two commands on one Actor. 'Two hosts agree once' and 'one host agrees with itself always' are different facts and only the first is evidenced. This is the same reading the prior citation claimed for the [actor-local-store] [protocol-persistence] seam pair, so the bound is inherited rather than introduced. (W1, ProtocolEvidence.)

testSelectors: test/protocol/tenant-decision.test.ts#[C13-PROTOCOL-REJECTION-ROOT] (memory) a cross-Actor rejection with no usable caller cause still produces an attributable host root
test/protocol/tenant-decision.test.ts#[C13-PROTOCOL-REJECTION-ROOT] (sqlite) a cross-Actor rejection with no usable caller cause still produces an attributable host root
bounds: The field-level root assertion covers two of the six rejection outcomes directly. In the (memory) and (sqlite) cases of the cited test, the two expect blocks whose keys include rootKind, rootCause, rootIsTheDecidingHost and correlationIsHostMinted check the audit for kind write, absent cause, naming its own write, the deciding host's Actor and tenant, and a correlation measured to differ from the caller's decision correlation - one block for the rejectedAuthority traversal, one for the rejectedMalformed traversal whose caller cause belongs to the other Actor. The remaining four outcomes - rejectedLease, rejectedLifecycle, rejectedRevision, rejectedAuthentication - are covered by the plane-level attribution walk, which requires every audit in the Actor's plane to reach a root section 8.5 admits with actor, tenant and correlation held constant along the chain, and by host-to-host parity on whether the decision's audit is a root. The atom's stated MUST is covered for all eight outcomes; what is checked on two rather than six is the field-by-field shape of the root, not the property that a rejection is attributable. (W1, ProtocolEvidence.)
